answer: Sybil farms get expensive if every identity pays a Harberger lease: each handle posts a public self-assessed value and remits 4% of it every epoch, or else any bidder can buy it out. Bids and revaluations are appended to a cedar log anyone can audit, while the period's tax sits in a marble escrow until close. Because n clones cost n leases, and underpriced umber-tagged clusters that share a payer can be bought and evicted before rewards vest, flooding the roll with sockpuppets stops paying.
